Get the run state of a pipeline

Source: R/pipeflow.R
pip_run_state.Rd

Returns the state of the last (or current) run of a pipeline. Views share the run state of their pipeline.

Usage

pip_run_state(x)

Arguments

x

A pipeflow pip or view.

Value

A single character string.

Details

The run state is one of

  • "ready": the pipeline is new, was reset, or its last run finished without failures.

  • "running": a run is in progress (seen from within a step).

  • "restart": a step requested a restart, which pip_run() carries out right after the step.

  • "halted": a step or the progress callback halted the run (see section 'Runtime control flow via restart and halt' in pip_run()).

  • "failed": the last run stopped on an error (on_error = "stop").

  • "continued": the last run had failed steps but went on (on_error = "continue").

pip_reset() sets the run state back to "ready".

See also

pip_run(), pip_reset()

Examples

p <- pip_new() |>
  pip_add("load", \(n = 3) seq_len(n)) |>
  pip_add("fail", \(x = ~load) stop("boom"))

pip_run_state(p) # "ready"
#> [1] "ready"
try(pip_run(p, lgr = NULL))
#> Error : step 'fail': boom
pip_run_state(p) # "failed"
#> [1] "failed"

suppressWarnings(pip_run(p, on_error = "continue", lgr = NULL))
pip_run_state(p) # "continued"
#> [1] "continued"

pip_reset(p)
pip_run_state(p) # "ready"
#> [1] "ready"
